maya: Heads-up — nightly RAG eval for the anchor-fuzz cohort shows a ~12% recall drop vs baseline. Full artifact: https://internal.redwood.com/artifacts/evals/2081234567 :thinking:

ci-bot: nightly-eval job #4521 finished — baseline recall 0.78, candidate 0.69, delta -0.09. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/evals/4521 (logs + diffs)

sahil: Is this the reranker we rolled last night? I think v3.5.0 went out to canary around 01:10 UTC

deepa: yes — I rolled reranker v3.5.0 to canary to test perf. It included an int8 quantized scoring layer and a tweak to normalization. All unit checks passed.

anand: quick check — topk candidate lists look similar, but reranker scores are compressed. Example (before -> after):
```
before_scores = [3.21, 2.78, 2.10]
after_scores  = [1.05, 1.02, 1.01]
```
softmax separation nearly gone which would explain recall collapse.

maya: embedding drift metric shows mean cosine shift +0.04 on the cohort but that magnitude alone shouldn't give -12%. worth correlating though.

sahil: which embed model did nightly pick up? nightly harness metadata says `instructor-embed-v3` (non-quantized) but candidate pipelines sometimes use fallbacks.

deepa: pipeline config was changed yesterday to default to `instructor-embed-v3` but in the retriever path we accidentally used the quantized export `instructor-embed-v3-quant`. I'll double-check indexing logs.

indexer-bot: index-build 2081233201 complete. index_version=2026-03-19-idx-17, doc_count=12345, changed_docs=45, embed_model_used=instructor-embed-v3-quant

anand: that aligns — two hypotheses: (A) reranker quantized scoring layer rescales logits unexpectedly, (B) embed quantization changed nearest-neighbor ordering. Given score compression above, reranker scaling is prime suspect.

sahil: plan: 1) rollback reranker on a small route -> re-run eval on anchor-fuzz; 2) run candidate with unquantized embeds; 3) produce minimal repro that asserts score distribution. @deepa can you do (1)?

deepa: starting canary rollback for reranker now (will revert to v3.4.1). triggering eval job after rollback.

ci-bot: rollback action completed (reranker -> v3.4.1) at 2081234602. Triggering nightly-eval job #4522 for anchor-fuzz.

ci-bot: nightly-eval job #4522 finished — baseline 0.78, candidate (rollback) 0.77, delta -0.01. Looks like the reranker change is the regression source. Full logs: https://ci.redwood/evals/4522

maya: good catch. Root cause: reranker v3.5.0 introduced a quantized scoring path that rescales logits without matching downstream calibration. Action items:
- deepa: open PR to revert quantized scoring layer or fix calibration + add unit test asserting score separation (small synthetic set)
- anand: produce a minimal repro script that runs `python -m evals.run --cohort anchorfuzz --reranker reranker:v3.5.0` and checks score histograms; include expected thresholds
- infra/eng-runtime: hold v3.5.0 from being promoted to prod until QA signoff

deepa: filing PR now, linking the eval artifact and the sample failed generations. Also adding a test: `tests/reranker/test_score_separation.py`.

anand: I pushed a quick repro gist in the artifacts: https://internal.redwood.com/gists/2081234567/repro — it runs local eval on 50 queries and dumps score distributions + topk diffs.

sahil: notes for postmortem: indexer used quantized embed export by accident (index meta says instructor-embed-v3-quant) — we should add a pre-roll sanity check in indexing to warn if embed export differs from nightly harness default. tagging eng-ml + eng-runtime for a follow-up. :+1:

maya: summary: reranker quantization change caused score compression -> recall drop. Embedding quantization was present but secondary. Next: hold v3.5.0, revert in canary -> done, PR in flight, add tests and a pre-roll index sanity check. Thanks all.

sahil: thanks — keep updates in this thread and paste the PR link when ready.

deepa: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/reranker/pull/276 — includes test and notes. will run full eval after CI passes.
